highlights: Resolved concurrent data overrides across 2 CRM modules (Accounts, Leads) by building a record locking mechanism, ensuring reliable multi-user audit tracking across 10+ workflows.
Built JWT-secured REST APIs for a role-based KPI dashboard, aggregating metrics across 4 database tables with real-time analytics and strict access control.
Stabilized CRM infrastructure by refactoring 10+ legacy cURL wrappers into standardized REST handlers, reducing HTTP 500/404 errors by 85% across staging environments.
Developed and refined React-based dashboard components to improve UI consistency and data visibility.
Integrated frontend with REST APIs and handled data inconsistencies to ensure smooth user experience.
Collaborated with backend developers to debug UI and data rendering issues during API integration.

features: Create multiple resumes with real-time preview
AI-enhanced Professional Summary and Experience Descriptions using Google Gemini API
Auto-extract resume fields from uploaded PDFs
Profile image upload with background removal via ImageKit integration

AI-Resume-Builder.design_tradeoffs: Chose Render free tier for backend causing initial spin-up latency (~50s delay on first request), but cost-effective. Used Gemini for AI features because it was faster and cheaper than OpenAI.
AI-Resume-Builder.what_i_would_do_differently: Implement WebSockets for real-time collaborative resume editing, and add more ATS (Applicant Tracking System) scoring integration directly in the builder.

QuickBlog-FullStack.design_tradeoffs: Deployed backend on Vercel Serverless which has a 10s execution timeout (cold start issue), but yields excellent cost-efficiency and scales to zero. Used standard JWT stored in HTTP-Only cookies for secure auth.
QuickBlog-FullStack.what_i_would_do_differently: Switch to Next.js to leverage Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) for fast blog rendering and better SEO, since search engine bots would index pre-rendered pages faster.

features: Predicts whether an individual earns >$50K/year based on demographic data (age, education, hours worked, occupation, etc.)
Full data analysis, preprocessing, and model selection in Jupyter notebook
Standardized ML pipeline (Scaling, Label Encoding, standard algorithms like XGBoost)
Flask web app interface to query predictions against serialized model (pickle)
Fully containerized Docker build deployed via GitHub Actions CI/CD to Docker Hub / hosting provider
Income-Predictor.design_tradeoffs: Used simple Flask server as the API layer rather than FastAPI because it was a lightweight model, and Flask was quick to configure for HTML templates. Serialized model as pickle, which has security implications (unpickling untrusted files), but fine for self-contained server.
Income-Predictor.what_i_would_do_differently: Use FastAPI for automatic OpenAPI documentation, asynchronous request handling, and type validation using Pydantic. Train an ensemble of XGBoost and LightGBM for improved accuracy.
